marcus: onboarding note — sable30b + int4 pack shows a subtle coherence break after an alternating-anchor prefill (patterned anchors separated by short free text).

marcus: repro:```bash
./tools/prefill_runner.py --model sable30b --quant int4pack --prefetch tiled --prefetch-stride 8 --rotate-mode compact --prompt tests/patterned_anchors.txt --max-tokens 8192
```

anya: can you share the failing sample? we can try running under qemu/avx2 and native to check arch differences.

marcus: failing pattern is attached inline (shortened): "AnchorA: X^4000 AnchorB: Y^4000 Followup: summarize difference" — with tiled prefetch+compact rotate the followup starts to drift syntactically and sometimes flips a fact.

zhou: did you try --no-kv-cache? if it goes away that's a clear KV-path issue.

marcus: yep, with --no-kv-cache the output matches baseline. so KV index / prefill interaction.

ops-bot: infra-deploy notice: nightly-prefill job for sable30b scheduled at 03:00 UTC.

marcus: trimmed logs from a failing run:```
[2025-09-02T08:17:02Z] prefill:start tokens=4096 anchors=2
[2025-09-02T08:17:02Z] prefill:write kv_start=4096 kv_end=8192 tiled:tile_idx=511 stride=8
[2025-09-02T08:17:03Z] gen:attn_offset=4096
[2025-09-02T08:17:03Z] WARN: rop_scale_delta=0.0009765625 (expected ~0)
[2025-09-02T08:17:03Z] ERROR: kv_index_calc=8183 computed_ring_idx=8191 mismatch
```

anya: rop_scale_delta nonzero suggests fractional accumulation somewhere. could be rotate math using floats then cast or mismatch between tokenizer and runtime rop base.

zhou: note we recently added an int4 memcpy pad that aligns to 16 bytes which changes tile bytesize. tiled prefetch code assumes tile byte length is multiple of warp_size, maybe off-by-pad.

marcus: quick experiments I ran:
- linear prefetch + legacy rotate -> no mismatch (3/3)
- tiled prefetch + compact rotate + quant=int4pack -> mismatch (10/10)
- tiled prefetch + compact rotate + quant=int8 -> no mismatch

zhou: that pattern strongly implicates int4 packing + tiled path. padding + integer division could drop fractional remainder and shift kv indices.

marcus: I tried adjusting runtime rop_scale to 0.999984 and drift reduced but still present. so this isn't pure rop param mismatch.

anya: can you paste the compute snippet where tile offset is computed? we had a recent micro-optim that inlined division and truncated.

marcus: snippet from runtime (simplified):```c
int compute_kv_offset(int base_token, int stride, int tile_idx) {
    // old: return base_token + stride * tile_idx;
    // micro-opt: use fast_div for stride bytes, then >> shift
    int bytes_per_token = (quant == INT4) ? (token_bytes/2) : token_bytes;
    int tile_bytes = bytes_per_token * stride;
    int tile_offset = (base_token * bytes_per_token) + (tile_idx * tile_bytes);
    return tile_offset / bytes_per_token; // integer division truncates
}
```

zhou: that final division after constructing byte offsets can truncate fractional bytes introduced by padding. if tile_bytes includes padding, dividing back will shift indices.

anya: fix options: 1) preserve integer math in token units (avoid round-trip into bytes) 2) add assertion that (tile_offset % bytes_per_token)==0 before dividing 3) maintain a padding-aware index path for packed quantizations.

marcus: proposed immediate actions: add assert + regression test for patterned_anchors under int4pack tiled prefetch; add a unit test for tile_offset invariants; gate compact rotate on a padding-aware prefetch path until fixed.

ci-bot: perf-smoke: queued 5 runs (sable30b-int4pack) across linux-x86_64 and linux-aarch64.

zhou: I'll draft a small PR to avoid the byte->token round-trip and keep everything in token units with checked multiplications. also add explicit pad accounting.

anya: I'll add a nightly regression in test-harness to run patterned_anchors at reduced length (4096) across quant knobs. ops-bot can help schedule. @ops-bot can you add a one-off job flagged critical for this week?

ops-bot: Created job prefill-regress/sable30b-int4pack-critical scheduled for 2025-09-03T03:00:00Z.

marcus: thanks. will attach failing seed + exact output diffs in the PR. also adding a small bisect to see when packed-mem-pad landed.

zhou: ping me on the PR, I'll run cross-arch repro (arm64) and check our memcpy variants.

marcus: sg, thanks all :) will post links here when PRs and CI runs are up. :rocket:
